paper.title: Predicting eventual development of lupus nephritis at the time of diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus

nodes.text: What factors at the time of SLE diagnosis predict future development of lupus nephritis?
nodes.anchor: To investigate factors predictive of future lupus nephritis development when systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is diagnosed.

nodes.text: Low albumin-to-globulin ratio (AGR) at SLE diagnosis is strongly associated with increased risk of future lupus nephritis development.
nodes.anchor: In particular, a low AGR (aHR 4.972, 95% CI: 2.394 – 10.326, p < 0.001) was strongly associated with an increased risk of future lupus nephritis development.

nodes.text: Young age, low C3, high anti-dsDNA titre, and presence of anti-Sm antibody at SLE diagnosis are associated with risk of future lupus nephritis.
nodes.anchor: Young age, low C3, high anti-dsDNA titre and presence of anti-Sm antibody at diagnosis of SLE were associated with a risk of future lupus nephritis

nodes.text: Low AGR has the greatest hazard for lupus nephritis among the predictive factors (aHR 4.972).
nodes.anchor: Notably, the factor associated with the greatest hazard for lupus nephritis was a low AGR (aHR 4.972, 95% CI: 2.394 – 10.326, p < 0.001).

nodes.text: AGR has the highest discrimination ability (AUC 0.769) for lupus nephritis development compared to albumin (AUC 0.754) and globulin (AUC 0.600).
nodes.anchor: AGR, with the highest AUC, had the highest discrimination ability for development of lupus nephritis among the three variables.

nodes.text: The cumulative incidence of lupus nephritis in Korean SLE patients is 34.8%.
nodes.anchor: Thus, the cumulative incidence of lupus nephritis was 34.8% (136 of 391)

nodes.text: Low AGR reflects a greater proportion of immunoglobulin relative to total protein, suggesting higher autoantibody burden.
nodes.anchor: one possible explanation is that a low AGR, indicating a greater proportion of globulin relative to total protein, reflects the higher amounts of antibodies in the serum of patients with SLE.

nodes.text: Anti-dsDNA antibody titre as a continuous variable shows a 4% increased risk of lupus nephritis per 100 IU/ml increase.
nodes.anchor: Based on the aHR, we estimated that risk of developing lupus nephritis increased by 4% per 100 IU/ml increase of anti-dsDNA titre.

nodes.text: The study is limited by its retrospective, single-center design in a Korean population, and AGR may be susceptible to measurement variability though less so as a ratio.
nodes.anchor: First, this study was retrospective in design, and was a single center study in Korea. Thus further studies are required with larger number of subjects from different ethnic populations to confirm the present results.

nodes.text: Of 278 SLE patients without nephritis at baseline, 37 developed biopsy-proven lupus nephritis during a median follow-up of 44.9 months.
nodes.anchor: Of 278 patients newly diagnosed with SLE during the study period but without lupus nephritis at that time, 241 did not and 37 did develop nephritis on follow-up. The median follow-up duration was 44.9 (range: 29.0 – 68.4) months.

nodes.text: Median time to lupus nephritis development was 30.1 months (range 16.2–54.7).
nodes.anchor: The median time to development of lupus nephritis was 30.1 (range: 16.2 – 54.7) months.

nodes.text: Patients who developed nephritis were significantly younger at diagnosis (28.4 vs 40.8 years), had lower serum albumin (3.24 vs 3.86 g/dl), lower AGR (0.801 vs 1.044), lower C3 (55.8 vs 87.3 mg/dl), lower C4 (9.2 vs 15.8 mg/dl), higher anti-dsDNA titre (97.0 vs 8.1 IU/ml), higher SLEDAI (13.0 vs 8.2), higher frequency of anti-Sm (31.3% vs 13.8%), anti-RNP (54.1% vs 28.7%), and anti-beta2 glycoprotein IgM (16.7% vs 5.6%), and received higher cumulative glucocorticoid dose.

nodes.text: Univariate analysis identified younger age, lower AGR, lower C3, lower C4, higher anti-dsDNA titre, and presence of anti-Sm and anti-RNP antibodies as significantly associated with increased risk of lupus nephritis.
nodes.anchor: On univariate analysis, factors significantly associated with an increased risk of developing lupus nephritis included younger age, lower AGR, lower C3, lower C4, higher anti-dsDNA titre and the presence of anti-Sm and anti-RNP antibodies (Table 2).

nodes.text: Multivariate analysis showed age (aHR 0.928, 95% CI 0.895–0.961), C3 (aHR 0.977, 95% CI 0.966–0.989), anti-dsDNA titre (aHR 1.004, 95% CI 1.000–1.007), anti-Sm antibody (aHR 2.097, 95% CI 1.040–4.229), and low AGR (aHR 4.972, 95% CI 2.394–10.326) as independent predictors.

nodes.text: Among 391 Korean SLE patients, 99 had nephritis at presentation and 37 developed nephritis during follow-up, yielding a cumulative incidence of 34.8%.

nodes.text: Retrospective cohort study of 278 newly diagnosed SLE patients without baseline nephritis at Asan Medical Center, Seoul (2005–2015), followed for development of biopsy-proven lupus nephritis.
nodes.anchor: The electronic medical records of patients who were diagnosed with SLE at a tertiary referral hospital in Seoul, South Korea between January 2005 and December 2015 were retrospectively reviewed.

nodes.text: Calculate albumin-to-globulin ratio (AGR) as albumin/(total protein − albumin).
nodes.anchor: AGR was calculated using the equation AGR = albumin/(total protein − albumin).

nodes.text: Cox proportional hazards regression with univariate screening (p<0.05) followed by multivariate analysis to identify independent predictors of lupus nephritis.
nodes.anchor: Cox proportional hazard model was used to identify predictors of lupus nephritis. Univariate analysis was performed for each variable, and variables found to be statistically significant (p < 0.05) were included in multivariate analysis.

nodes.text: Assess proportional hazards assumption via log[−log(survival)] curves and Schoenfeld residuals.
nodes.anchor: The proportional hazards assumption was confirmed by examination of log[−log(survival)] curves and by testing Schoenfeld partial residuals, and no relevant violations were found.

nodes.text: Evaluate model discrimination using Harrell's c-index.
nodes.anchor: The discrimination ability of the multivariable model was evaluated using Harrell's overall c index.

nodes.text: Perform ROC analysis to determine optimal cut-off values for albumin, globulin, and AGR.
nodes.anchor: Receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis was performed, and the best cut-off value was determined.

nodes.text: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank test to compare nephritis-free survival by AGR cut-off.
nodes.anchor: Survival rates were analysed using the Kaplan–Meier method and were compared using the log-rank test.

nodes.text: Diagnose lupus nephritis by kidney biopsy classified per ISN/RPS 2003 system, with biopsy indicated per ACR recommendations (proteinuria ≥1 g/24h or ≥0.5 g/24h plus haematuria ≥5 RBCs/HPF or cellular casts).

nodes.text: Classify SLE per ACR 1997 criteria.
nodes.anchor: All patients met the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) classification criteria for SLE [13].

nodes.text: Assess disease activity using SLEDAI.
nodes.anchor: The SLE Disease Activity Index, a validated measure of lupus disease activity [14], was assessed at the time SLE was diagnosed.
